Money day: full plates. Thirty days later, up to fifteen percent fewer calories.
An economist studied food diaries from American families on food stamps.
The benefit landed on the same day every month. No surprise.
Yet calories fell a little every single day after it arrived. About ten to fifteen percent over the month.
And by week four, more families would take less than fifty dollars today, over fifty dollars next month.
Week one just feels more urgent than week four.
So split the money by week. Day thirty deserves a full plate too.
